hooks.name: Auto Documentation Update on Session Stop

action.prompt:
Check if the latest commit needs doc updates. Be economical — most commits do NOT.

STEP 1 — Cheap guard (do this first, one command only):
Run `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` (initial commit: `git show HEAD --stat`).
If EVERY changed path matches any of these, STOP immediately and reply exactly `No doc update needed.` — do NOT read any files, do NOT run more commands:
  - `.kiro/**` (hooks, steering, settings)
  - `docs/**` or `employeeapi/docs/**` (already docs)
  - `**/*Test.java` or `**/test/**` (tests only)
  - `*.md`, `.github/**`, `postman/**`, lockfiles
Also STOP with `No doc update needed.` if the diff is empty.

STEP 2 — Only if real code/config changed (src, entities, controllers, security, Dockerfile, docker-compose, pom.xml):
Run `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` and identify what changed: endpoints/contracts, data model/schema, security/auth, deployment/env, architecture/dependencies, or performance-relevant code.

STEP 3 — Read ONLY the docs mapped to what changed (not all docs):
  endpoints/contracts → docs/api-contract.md, employeeapi/docs/api.md
  data model/schema → docs/data-model-uml.md, employeeapi/docs/diagrams/*
  security/auth → employeeapi/docs/security.md, security-implementation.md
  deployment/env/Docker → docs/contianerization-guide.md, employeeapi/docs/deployment.md
  architecture/deps → docs/backend-plan.md, employeeapi/docs/architecture.md
  build/dev workflow → employeeapi/docs/development.md
  Swagger/OpenAPI → docs/swagger-guide.md
  new major feature → employeeapi/docs/index.md
  performance → employeeapi/docs/performance.md

STEP 4 — Make targeted updates only: preserve existing tone/structure, change only affected sections, keep it factual (document what the code does).

STEP 5 — Report briefly: which files changed and why. If nothing needed updating, say so.
